artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $p$ be a prime and let $q$ be a power of $p$. Recall that a finite group $G$ is called $p$-solvable if every composition factor of $G$ is either a $p$-group or a group of order coprime to $p$. For a $p$-solvable group $G$, the (upper) $p$-series is defined inductively by $1 = P_0(G) \trianglelefteq O_{p'}(G) = N_0(G) \trianglelefteq P_1(G) \trianglelefteq N_1(G) \trianglelefteq \cdots$, where $P_{i+1}(G)/N_i(G) = O_p(G/N_i(G))$ and $N_{i+1}(G)/P_{i+1}(G) = O_{p'}(G/P_{i+1}(G))$; the $p$-length $\ell_p(G)$ is the smallest integer $k$ such that $P_k(G) = N_k(G) = G$.

For each positive integer $n$, define
$$m_n(q) = \max\{ \ell_p(H) : H \le \mathrm{GL}(n,q),\ H \text{ is } p\text{-solvable}\}.$$

Determine whether
$$\lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{m_n(q)}{\log_2 n} = 1.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed by İ. Güloğlu as a new entry in the Kourovka Notebook of unsolved problems in group theory. A targeted web search did not find a published resolution; classical bounds on p-length (Hall–Higman type) give logarithmic order, but the precise asymptotic constant equal to 1 has not been verified in available literature.
